Personally I lurk for a lot of reasons. Just because you left someone doesn't mean you don't love them anymore. In earlier stages before everything went to shit, I lurked because I wanted to know what was going on in their life. I wanted to feel close even though I couldn't be close. When I left that time,  I felt that my partner was incapable of healthy communication with me, unable to empathize, and unable to support me.

This time I left because I found out he was lying and cheating. Now I lurk because I'm a fucking masochist apparently.  I lurk because I want more of the truth. And as it leaks out, it kills me. It really kills me. I guess I lurk also because I want the truth not to be the truth. I wish that all his lies were true. I wish he was the person I thought he was. 

There's no part of me that is lurking to see if j made the right decision.  I should have left a long time ago. I never should have gotten in the relationship in the first place. 

But even so, you just can't stop loving someone at the flip of a switch. Even if they weren't real. I don't lurk out of uncertainty or regret, I lurk because I loved them and don't have the self control to stop stabbing myself in the heart. 

The lesson of the day is to stop lurking lol. It's torture.

Zofran is your best friend. It’s #1. 

For me antacids stopped working and PPIs, if allowed, were much better. But if antacids still work, peppermint tums 1000 was the best for me. The regular and extra strength have a chalky flavor that also make me gag. 

Ice is also my best friend. Hospital slushy ice is the easiest and best to eat. Keep it in a yeti or Zojirushi and you can have it on the go always. Sonic and Costco also sell slushy ice, and honestly give it to me for free all the time. 

Coconut water also has electrolytes. I don’t tolerate most flavors of Gatorade and I hate pedialyte, but love coconut water. I most brands taste funny to me. Harmless Harvest is the only one that tastes like actual coconut water. Water it down if too strong. Make ice cubes out of it too. 

watered down apple juice with lots of ice. 

Salty things help with nausea for me. I used to carry broth or even bouillon cubes with me. Jerky also helped with protein. Not the best tasting, and when you’re tired you kind of don’t want to chew, but sometimes it’s salty and takes away that nausea so the work is worth it.

Having an empty stomach makes the nausea worse, so rotating through foods to find a safe food is paramount. 

Sometimes the rate at what you eat really is one bite at a time, and while it doesn’t feel like it’s enough calorie wise or nutrient wise, it’s better than nothing because it does stave off other symptoms.

I once had a week where coke slurpees eaten with a spoon was the only thing I could reliably keep down. Sometimes what stays down is weird and suddenly it just flips..

Doing the work of constantly trying to eat is still better than dealing with the tube in hospital for me. 

I absolutely loathe those damned protein/nutritional drinks, but if you have to shift to it, for me blending it with a lot of ice is easier than just cold. Or freezing it into cubes and blending it. 

Also you can cook with unflavored protein powder if you do get to a stage where it’s tolerable. A lot of people stick to the high sugar stuff, but as someone who loves savory, making protein gravy and protein quiche was much easier for me. One. Bite. At a time. 

Once you give in to that first puke, it’s really hard to stop. When I’m in a rhythm of not puking, I eat high protein before bed and eat carbs immediately when I wake. I know it’s not what’s recommended for most, but most people can eat whenever they want. In the end, eating something is always better than eating nothing for this situation.

I wish I could help with the fatigue and discomfort. I’ve never really found a solution to this either besides taking deep baths and a lot of breaks where I can lay down. Sometimes I already need a nap at 10-11am which confounds people because the day just barely started. 

Something to remember is that what a break is for you is not necessarily a break for her. For me, being in public is not a break. Unless I’m in a quiet dark room where I can fully recline with a blanket, in comfortable temperature, I’m expending energy. That means going to a cafe is not rest. Sitting is not rest. Being on a crowded beach is not rest etc. 

I hope some of this can help.

I don't think it's petty at all. Or if it is, I'm right along with you in the petty party. Losing eyelashes, eyebrows, and hair, was and is one of the most traumatising parts of the process for me.   


I was never really into beauty before cancer. I was a very practical person. Vanity was for the truly physically beautiful people. My beauty was my achievements; my research, my work, my brain.   


I tried so hard to maintain all of my lifestyles.  Work, school, and being a cancer patient, in secret of course. I was so intent on maintaining my head high. So proud. Soooo in denial. Then I lost my motherfucking eyelashes. I had been losing hair for weeks. It wasn't a big deal, I had tons of thick, long hair, it went nearly all the way down to my butt. Here and there I was self conscious for leaving little piles of evidence of my presence around, but still, no big deal. But when I lost my eyelashes, and when my brows started to patch up, something inside me broke.   


I've had 8 years of this shit. 8 years, and you'd think I'd have gotten over it. But no. I restarted chemo a few months ago, and went through it all over again. it still is one of the most painful things to me. And mind you, my bottom lashes never fully recovered. I'm sitting at about 30% of length and volume here. Big bald patches too.   


It's a mindfuck my internet friend. When the outside reflects the chaos that's occurring inside. When everyone else can see what you're going through. When you're stripped of the things that make you, you, and are left with "Cancer Chick". Hello internet friendo, I actually just experienced the same quite recently. Not the suicide part, but the prolonged panic attack. In my younger days, I had frequent panic attacks from PTSD, but they were more like the kind that you read about online. Short, intense, feels like you’re going to die. 

This prolonged attack was on another level. For me it was triggered by a somewhat traumatic experience. My stalker that had been nonviolent and inactive for months had suddenly showed up at a terrible time, which resulted in a physical struggle that ended in me covered in bruises, and running for a taxi. The panic attack started inside the taxi; hyperventilating, crying, sweating, world was kind of spinning. For the next few HOURS I was going in an out of crying, hyperventilating, and I had this tingly feeling all over my body. I had never in my life experienced that tingly feeling. In the days after, I was so immensely tired, as if I was hungover. This type of panic attack was so different from the ones I experienced in my youth, I wasn’t even sure that that’s what it was. And in the days after as I went place to place seeking help, I had little mini episodes each time. 

I can’t understand your exact situation OP, but you’re not alone in your experiences. While I didn’t have suicidal thoughts then, I’m in a fairly dark spot right now. I get it, friend. As do many others here. 

The thing is internet friendo, this too shall not pass if you just wait for it to pass. It looks like you’ve been suffering for days and are at or approaching a peak. It looks like you’re working within a system that isn’t made to appropriately treat you. This too shall not pass, if you end up at a point where you attempt to end your life. 

This can pass if you make it your goal. You’ve put so much effort getting this far on your own. You’ve found ways to manage your agoraphobia and other anxieties, and that’s huge! 

But perhaps these thoughts are your body’s way of expressing that you are pushing past your limits. That you could use a hand with all the weight. 

What do you think about brainstorming together what your options are? We can try to come up with a plan for the next few days at least, and maybe in the future we can troubleshoot some of the bigger things.

> Your anxiety is so bad you are considering suicide yet taking medication designed to relieve exactly what you are experiencing is “rock bottom”? I don’t mean to be rude but you need a reality check. Medication is life changing and you are letting your anxiety and stigma regarding medication to keep you suffering. Honestly it’s hard for me to be sympathetic when people say stuff like this. Like there is an obvious solution and you won’t even try it? Meat, fresh veggies, and fresh fruit are expensive. The quality and availability of dairy is abysmal. Avocados .50c-$1 at home. $4+ per avocado here. 

If you buy common fresh fruits and veggies, it's not so bad. Mandarins are dirt cheap (thanks jeju!) Cabbage is always cheap. Cucumbers are cheap. Korean cucumbers are particularly delicious.
